answer: Each new agent identity must lock a deposit that grows with every additional identity the same operator creates: like stacking marble slabs, each fake costs more than the last, so a sybil farmer bleeds capital before gaining influence. The deposit is refunded only after a long window of honest behavior, and misbehavior slashes it. A copper-bound signing key ties each identity to one tamper-evident history, and only identities carrying a strong verified signal of past honest work may join critical quorums, so cheap fresh identities cannot steer decisions.
